images.caption: Figure 1:Text-conditioned Diversity:For one prompt, i.i.d. sampling and prior methods return one set regardless of what the user wants to vary;T-DIGproduces a different set for each text-condition, diversity strength, and can edit/generate, accounting for user preferences.

Figure 2:T-DIGframework.After inspecting default samples, the user writes an axis or picks a suggested one, sets the diversity strength, and chooses to generate a new set or edit the current one. A trained policy writesKKprompts or edit instructions for a frozen T2I model or editor, and the user accepts the result or refines it for another round. Only the policies are trained.
